subject: Recap: PayBridge integration discussion — usage economics & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Simmons <alex@paybridge.com>, Kimberly Ross <kimberly.ross@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: PayBridge integration discussion — usage economics & next steps

Alex / Kimberly — thanks again for the 60m earlier. Quick written recap so we have aligned next steps and to surface the concrete economics we discussed. High-level notes and asks below.

1) Key pain points you reiterated
- Token-driven cost variability: spikes on settlement windows create surprise spend and make budgeting difficult.
- Tail latency at peak loads impacts UX during reconciliation flows (15–20% of requests seeing >300ms).
- Audit footprint & retention: need clear logs and easy export for finance/regulatory reviews.

2) Goals you want to hit in 2028
- Cap inference spend to a predictable band (target: $250k–$350k annual for inference initially).
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost by 35%–50% without regressing latency SLAs.
- Proof-of-value within a 6–8 week pilot and measurable unit-economics report.

3) Cost levers and quick wins we discussed
- Request-level batching (synchronous batching for non-interactive reconciliation paths) — expected 20–35% token reduction per effective throughput increase.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (payment status checks) — ~10–25% token savings depending on cache hit rate.
- Model routing: route low-risk, high-volume flows to a smaller quantized model variant.
- Autoscaling + Reserved Dedicated nodes for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale.

4) Proposed mutual action plan (milestones)
- This week: you share a 7-day sample trace & budget guardrails (what you can commit to for pilot spend).
- Next 7 days: Redwood runs a quick sim (attached spreadsheet) and returns a 3-scenario TCO (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with expected savings from batching/cache.
- Week 3–6: Pilot (sandbox dataset, canary traffic, telemetry/SLAs).
- Week 7–8: ROI readout and decision on expand/reserved capacity.

5) Quick ask for you now
- Can you confirm the budget band you mentioned on the call? You said roughly mid-six figures annually — please confirm the target annual budget for inference we should model (short answer: $___).

Attached: preliminary modeling template I used in the call (paybridge_usage_modeling.xlsx) and a short simulation summary (redwood_batching_simulation.pdf).

If this aligns I’ll schedule a 30m walkthrough with Marissa (solutions) and our infra PM to kick off the sim.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Budget: we are working off a $300k annual target for inference; flexibility for pilot spend is +/- 20% but any longer-term committed spend would need CFO sign-off.
- Traffic profile: the 7-day trace will include a heavy reconciliation window on weekdays (peaks ~ 18:00–20:00 PST) and lighter loads on weekends. I’ll attach an anonymized sample of the trace by EOD.
- Batching question: can you give a short example of latency tradeoffs? For example, if we batch reconciliation calls into 50–100ms windows, what happens to p95 latency for interactive flows?

If you can return the sim by Friday that would be great — Kimberly and I will review with ops.

Alex — appreciate the fast turnaround and the $300k guidance, that’s exactly what we needed to model. Attached is the sim we promised and a short TCO sketch for three scenarios (all numbers are rough until we run the pilot with your trace):

Executive summary (ballpark, monthlyized)
- Current: baseline internal estimate (using your current provider) — $32k/month inferred for the flows you shared.
- Redwood Hosted (no commit): $28k/month (higher per-unit, flexible, good for POC).
- Redwood Dedicated (6–12 month reserved capacity): $17k/month — ~40% reduction vs Hosted once utilization crosses ~60%.

Savings drivers and conservative impact modeling
- Batching (synchronous 50–150ms windows on reconciliation batch jobs): expected 20–30% token savings; p95 latency for interactive flows unchanged because we only batch non-interactive reconciliation traffic and keep interactive routes on low-latency paths.
- Prefix/KV cache (50–70% hit on common lookup prompts): incremental 12–18% token reduction on those flows.
- Model routing / quantization (route low-risk flows to a 4-bit quantized variant): conservative 10–15% unit-cost reduction per token.

Combined conservative estimate: 35–50% total unit-cost reduction vs your current baseline after pilot + routing/batching adoption.

Attachments included:
- paybridge_usage_modeling.xlsx (worksheet: raw trace / scenario calculators)
- redwood_batching_simulation.pdf (short charts & assumptions)

Quick next steps I’ll do this week:
- Run the sim with your 7-day trace once you drop it into the Drive link.
- Marissa will schedule a 30m technical run to discuss batching windows and routing rules.

If that sounds right I’ll lock a time for the tech walk-through.

Thanks,
Karthik
